messages.author: 1ebe9f0f5834d2d6
messages.subject: dist.breaks and histogram
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm having a minor issue creating a histogram based on a distsamp
output. It's a relatively minor issue but it's bugging me. How do I
get the histogram bars to be centered over a number? The way my
histogram looks it implies that I estimated distance out to 6 m, which
I didn't do.

I think I have entered my data correctly but I will recap below.

For this study I used line transects and estimated the distance of
butterflies to the nearest meter, out to 5 m. I entered
dist.breaks=c(0,1,2,3,4,5,6) into unmarkedFrameDS along with all of
the other information. I run a null model and get back reasonable
estimates. But when creating the histogram I get the bars above the
meter marks are offset and not directly over the scale numbers. This
makes it look like I estimated distance out to 5.5 m.

Assuming I entered the data correctly, any ideas on how to fix the
histogram so that I the bars line up over the meter marks?

Thanks

Chris

funkytown = unmarkedFrameDS(y=cbind(ds4t$D0, ds4t$D1, ds4t$D2, ds4t
$D3, ds4t$D4, ds4t$D5), siteCovs=data.frame(ds4t$Site,ds4t$Temp, ds4t
$RH, ds4t$Habitat), dist.breaks=c(0,1,2,3,4,5,6), tlength=ds4t$Length,
survey='line', unitsIn='m')
fmt.1 = distsamp(~1 ~1, funktown)
hist(fmt.1, xlab='Distance (m)', main='', col='grey')

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] dist.breaks and histogram
parts:
Hi Chris,

If you estimated distance out to 5 m, then you should use dist.breaks=c(0,1,2,3,4,5). These define the distance intervals. In this case there are 5 intervals and so your "y" matrix should have 5 columns corresponding to the counts of butterflies in each distance interval. Does this clear things up?

Richard

messages.subject: Re: dist.breaks and histogram
parts:
OK, my problem was that I entered my data as precise distances rather
than bins of data.

I corrected my problem and binned my data as follows:

D0 : 0 - 0.9m
D1: 1 - 1.9 m
D2: 2 - 2.9 m
D3: 3 - 3.9 m
D4: 4 - 5 m

Thanks to Richard for his help.

Chris
